name: The Shattering of the Shadow Anchor
location: Dining Hall and Courtyard, Shadow Estate
result: Strategic Victory — Anchor destroyed, color and fire magic restored

casualties.attackers: Archie (temporarily lost his dignity floating like a feather)
casualties.defenders: The Shadow Anchor (SHATTERED), Orangus Cornelius (severe blunt force trauma and silver poisoning)

summary: This is the climax of the infamous Shadow Estate dinner party. Stripped of his fire magic, Archie Miser had to rely on Bowser's fists and Green T's absolute ruthlessness. The battle involved a giant vampire bat, a defenestration, and Green T sniping a magical purple crystal hidden inside a hollow statue. The destruction of the Anchor brought color and fire back to the Shadowfell. Waluigi was not there, but he considers this the single greatest piece of property damage in the campaign's history, and Waluigi knows property damage.
description:
Waluigi must remind the reader of the stakes: Archie Miser woke up on a marble floor without his magic. The Shadowfell's entropy was so high, and its energy so low, that Archie couldn't even conjure a spark. Waluigi finds the idea of Archie without fire hilarious, but practically speaking, it meant Disaster Inc. was walking into a vampire lord's dining room completely unarmed. Except for Bowser, who is genetically a weapon, and Green T, who had apparently smuggled a flintlock pistol in his trousers.

**Phase 1: The Raw Meat and the Ultimatum**
The dinner began with Orangus Cornelius serving raw, dripping meat. Bowser ate it in one bite because Bowser has the palate of a garbage disposal. Cornelius then demanded a debt from Archie for burning his greenhouse in the material plane. This is typical aristocratic behavior—they invite you to dinner, serve you terrible food, and then ask you to pay for landscaping. When Cornelius threatened to turn Bowser's shell into a soup bowl, diplomacy officially ended.

Green T, sitting at the CHILDREN'S TABLE wearing a bib, kicked his table over, drew his weapon, and declared he had the key to the 'Anchor'. Cornelius panicked. This was the moment Waluigi wishes he could have painted and hung in the Louvre.

**Phase 2: The Defenestration of Cornelius**
Bowser flipped the main dining table, sending raw meat and coagulated blood-wax flying. Archie, realizing he was useless in a magical fight, grabbed a silver candlestick and actually hit a vampire with it. Waluigi respects the improvisation. Silver burns vampires, which is a universally known fact that vampires arrogantly ignore until someone hits them with the tableware.

Bowser then tackled Orangus Cornelius straight through the dining room window and into the courtyard. Waluigi has thrown people out of rings, off karts, and into bottomless pits, but tackling a vampire lord through a gothic window is objectively excellent showmanship.

**Phase 3: The Bat and the Crystal**
In the courtyard, Cornelius revealed his true form: a giant bat monster. Bowser, unfazed, simply bit the bat's wing. Waluigi wants to note that biting a giant undead bat requires a level of immune system confidence that Waluigi does not possess. 

Archie jumped out the window to help, but because the Shadowfell's gravity is fundamentally broken, he floated down slowly like a dandelion. Undignified! But this slow descent allowed Archie to see the battlefield from a tactical angle. When Bowser threw Cornelius into a winged statue, the statue shattered, revealing it was hollow. Inside pulsed a glowing purple crystal. The Anchor.

**Phase 4: The Shot**
Archie realized the crystal was maintaining the plane's suppression. He yelled for Bowser to smash it, but Cornelius lunged to protect it. Time slowed down. Green T, standing at the shattered window above like a sniper in a tuxedo, took aim. 

The bullet hit the crystal. The Anchor shattered into dust.

The effect was instantaneous. Reality cracked. Colors—reds, oranges, yellows—bled violently back into the monochrome world. The planar suppression collapsed. Archie felt heat return to his hands and immediately ignited. The Shadow Estate's absolute control over the local dimension was broken. Disaster Inc. had successfully lobotomized a vampire stronghold, and they did it before dessert.
aftermath: The shattering of the Shadow Anchor permanently altered the local physics of the Shadow Estate. Color returned, making the gothic architecture look incredibly tacky in Waluigi's opinion. More importantly, it restored the party's magical capabilities. Orangus Cornelius was severely wounded, opening the door for Vivian's succession claim and throwing the Onyx Hand into utter chaos. It also attracted the Mages' Guild, who showed up to 'manage the anomaly' and immediately started billing people for property damage. Typical.

reputationNotes.bowser: Bowser's brute force secured a strategic victory and impressed the Mages' Guild.
reputationNotes.green_t: Green T's tactical brilliance earned respect from both allies and enemies, but also cost him friends within the Onyx Hand.
reputationNotes.waluigi: Waluigi found the destruction of the Shadow Anchor hilarious, further cementing Disaster Inc.'s reputation for property damage.

imageCaption: The courtyard below the defenestration: the bat wheeling, and the purple crystal cracked through.

name: Skirmish in the Mazebound Grove
result: Survival — Party escaped, but Dan was captured

casualties.defenders: Parallel Dan (Captured), Party Morale (damaged by terrible rhyming)

summary: Waluigi hates musicals. He especially hates musicals where the chorus tries to strangle you. Markop's rescue team was ambushed in a petrified hedge maze by the 'Mazebound'—grey-skinned ghouls who sing theatrical patter-songs while ripping you apart. The party survived, but Dan was dragged away into the hedges. Waluigi considers this the most undignified battle of the campaign.
description:
After the Shadow Anchor shattered, the estate's grounds became even more hostile. Markop, leading Remi, Dan, Salam, and Eager, ventured into the estate's hedge maze looking for Archie. Instead of Archie, they found the Mazebound.

**The Ambush**
The Mazebound are hunched, snub-nosed humanoids with glowing white eyes and sharp nails. But their physical threat is secondary to their psychological warfare: they sing. They leaped out of the hedges doing 'jazz hands' and immediately launched into a rhyming chorus: 'Welcome to the grove, welcome to the gray! You'll never find the fountain so you might as well stay!'

Waluigi finds this deeply offensive. If you are going to taunt your enemies, do it with a sharp laugh or a magnificent monologue. Do not do a choreographed routine in a hedge maze.

**The Choreographed Violence**
The fight was chaotic. The Mazebound encircled the party, specifically targeting their weaknesses while singing a rapid patter-song: 'Check the Turtle! Big and loud! Check the Archer! Check the Whip! Check the Toads—one blue, one green? Or is he purple? Is he mean?'

Markop, proving his absolute pragmatism, ignored the music and coated his sword in an 'undead remedy.' When a Mazebound lunged, Markop struck, melting the creature's grey skin off its bones. Remi, still suffering from blood loss, tried to stab a Mazebound, but her dagger had no effect on its thick skin. The creature mocked her, attempting to give her a 'goodbye kiss' before Remi dodged and Salam provided covering fire.

**The Abduction of Dan**
The tragedy of this skirmish was Dan. Or rather, the 'Parallel Dan'. While Markop was bashing heads and Eager was tripping ghouls with his whip, the Mazebound swarmed Dan. They dragged him backward into the impenetrable petrified hedges. 

Bowser arrived moments later, entirely missing the musical number, and completely incinerated a section of the maze with his fire breath. But it was too late. Dan was gone, and the Mazebound retreated into the shadows, leaving only the echo of their terrible singing.
aftermath: The party was forced to press forward without Dan, deeply unnerved by the encounter. They eventually found the groundskeeper's cottage and discovered Archie's discarded pouch and watch, proving Archie had survived but was on the run. Waluigi hopes he never has to fight the Mazebound. Waluigi refuses to participate in a duet with a zombie.

reputationNotes.waluigi: Waluigi considers this the most undignified battle, deeply offended by the Mazebound's musical taunts.
reputationNotes.markop: Markop's pragmatism shines as he coats his sword in an undead remedy to defeat the Mazebound.
reputationNotes.remi_akamatsu_full_backstory: Remi's dagger proves ineffective against the Mazebound, lowering her standing among her allies.

imageCaption: The Mazebound come down the petrified hedge in formation, singing. The chorus line is not a figure of speech.

name: The Petrification of Remi
result: Remi petrified; status of Oracle's Deck unknown; rescue required

casualties.defenders: Remi petrified; one bloody toadburt 'erased' by the Archivist

summary: What began as a search for Archie became a coordinated trap. Imps led Remi to a locked room. The Archivist threatened to kill her friends with transformed monsters. Bowser retreated to save lives. Guards blocked every exit except one. That exit led to a medusa's workshop. Remi is now stone. The Oracle's Deck—prophecy cards of significant power—are with her or nearby. Rescue is urgent. Time may be limited.
description:
Waluigi documents this event with the urgency it deserves. Remi is PETRIFIED. This is not a metaphor for being scared. She has been turned to STONE by a medusa's gaze and is currently a statue in a workshop full of statues.

## Sequence of Events

### Day 1: The Setup

The Onyx Hand guards had been behaving strangely around Remi:

**The 'Cure':** Guards claimed they would cure Remi of 'purpleeyetus'—the toads were skeptical, but Remi trusted them because 'they said they were going to help.'

**The Ring:** A guard delivered a letter 'from your vampire friends' containing a 'friendship ring.' The letter used handwriting Remi recognized from a guest book. The ring leaked faint smoke. Remi kept it.

**The Anklet:** When Remi declined a second ring, guards offered a 'friendship anklet.' Remi declined due to no accompanying letter. The guards were PERSISTENT.

**The 'Accident':** A guard 'tripped' into Remi, cutting her eye with a gash—just as Markop was asking to examine her eyes. Convenient timing.

**Strategic Repositioning:** Guards moved into blocking positions: 5 at the corner door, 5 cornering toads, 5 blocking Bowser, Markop, and Remi. Battle seemed imminent.

**Marcus Ashford's Intervention:** The Onyx Hand representative appeared, de-escalated the situation, gave Remi a potion that turned her eyes blue (curing the purple condition), and pickpocketed a letter from Bowser.

### Day 2: The Trap Springs

Remi's ring leaked black smoke. Guards claimed it needed 'recharging' due to 'leaking entropy.'

Markop completed a ritual revealing:
- The ring contained necromancy magic
- Another ring in Remi's pocket contained destructive magic
- Magical signatures in the walls suggested surveillance

The toads observed Marcus steal Bowser's paper but said nothing until later—triggering confrontation when Bowser noticed his missing paperwork.

Marcus taunted everyone with rhyming verse, read part of Bowser's letter aloud, and mocked the 'three-eyed failure' (Archie), the 'dwarf and toads,' and Bowser's lost throne.

The group decided to find Archie at the airship. Marcus claimed Archie's 'eyes rolled so far back he lost the plot.'

### The Library Trap

Remi headed downstairs to the library. Imps claimed they had 'found Archie' and led her to a room.

The room was locked.

Bowser shouted 'REMI NO' and busted down the door. He grabbed an imp and crushed it—blood emerged, confirming they were real creatures. He threw the corpse to a flower plant.

Remi entered the Archivist's room. The door locked behind her.

The Archivist snapped his fingers and declared:
- She was 'free to go'
- Her friends would 'die at the hands of imps'
- He had 'erased' a bloody toadburt found in the room
- He told 'FNG' to leave

Bowser saw the imps transform into giants, demons, and monsters. Overwhelming force.

The Archivist smiled as he 'led Remi to the exit door.'

Bowser thought: 'I don't want these people to die. Hjumpik wouldn't like this.' He left the grand entrance open and retreated—allowing others to escape the transformed creatures.

### The Workshop

Remi found only one way forward. Guards blocked every door. She was alone.

One door remained: the workshop.

She entered.

Lyranth waited—a medusa with marble-pale skin covered in vibrant paint, crown of snakes swaying, surrounded by her partially-completed masterpieces. Statues of stunning artistry. Statues that were once people.

Lyranth glared at Remi.

She said: 'Smile.'

Remi turned to stone.

## Critical Assets at Risk

**The Oracle's Deck:** Remi possesses magical tarot cards that predict the future—cards that showed Hjumpik navigating the Maze of Time, Markop wrestling the Arachnid Matriarch, and Lady Aurelian Corvinarus in the Feywild. These cards are significant prophetic artifacts.

- Are they petrified with Remi?
- Did they fall when she transformed?
- Can they function while their bearer is stone?

**Intelligence:** Remi gathered significant information throughout the estate—Ryan's diary, guard patterns, power dynamics. This intelligence is now inaccessible.

**The Rings:** Remi possessed at least two magical rings—one necromantic, one destructive. These artifacts are now with her statue.

## Rescue Parameters

Medusa petrification has varying reversibility:

**Time Sensitivity:** Some petrification becomes permanent after hours or days. Immediate action may be critical.

**Reversal Methods:** Specific spells, alchemical agents, or medusa-specific countermeasures might reverse the transformation.

**Lyranth's Cooperation:** The medusa herself might be able to reverse her work—if persuaded, threatened, or bargained with.

**Estate Resources:** The Shadow Estate's infirmary or other facilities might possess reversal capabilities—though trusting estate resources seems inadvisable given who orchestrated the trap.

## Rescue Challenges

**Location Unknown:** Bowser, Markop, and the toads fled transformed monsters. They may not know Remi entered the workshop. They may not know she's petrified.

**The Archivist:** The orchestrator remains active, commands transformed creatures, and has demonstrated willingness to 'erase' people.

**Lyranth:** Even if rescuers reach the workshop, they face a medusa. Looking at her means petrification. Fighting her requires not looking. This is difficult.

**Succession Crisis:** The broader estate remains in chaos. Vivian hunts through corridors. Guards have divided loyalties. Resources are contested.

## Waluigi's Assessment

This was not random violence. This was a COORDINATED TRAP:

1. Isolate Remi from allies
2. Threaten allies with overwhelming force to ensure separation
3. Block all exits except one
4. Funnel victim to Lyranth
5. Petrify

The Archivist orchestrated this. Lyranth executed it. The guards facilitated it. Someone wanted Remi neutralized specifically—possibly for the Oracle's Deck, possibly for her gathered intelligence, possibly for reasons not yet apparent.

Rescue is URGENT. Waluigi cannot help directly from the Feywild. The toads, Bowser, and Markop must realize Remi is missing, deduce her location, and mount a rescue operation against a medusa in a vampire estate during a succession crisis while transformed monsters roam the corridors.

The odds are not good. But Disaster Inc. has survived worse odds. Waluigi has to believe they'll find a way.

WAH.
aftermath: Remi remains petrified. Her allies are scattered, potentially unaware of her fate. The Archivist's trap succeeded. Lyranth has a new potential sculpture. Time is unknown but likely limited.

reputationNotes.bowser: King of the Koopas withdrew in time but now faces a petrified ally.
reputationNotes.remi_akamatsu_full_backstory: Artificer Remi is now a statue due to Shadow Estate's trap.
reputationNotes.waluigi: Archivist Waluigi orchestrated the successful trap, earning respect from his faction while alienating others.
reputationNotes.markop: Markop tried to help but was unsuccessful; he lost a fellow toad to the enemy.

imageCaption: Lyranth's workshop with one more statue in it than it had that morning. The Oracle's Deck is somewhere in this room.

name: The Dinner's Climax: The Vote
result: Orangus Cornelius shot with silver; Vivian claims title of Heir

casualties.attackers: Usk (finger severed by Archie as proof of loyalty — Waluigi has FEELINGS about this)
casualties.defenders: Orangus Cornelius (shot with silver bullet by Green T)

summary: The Shadow Estate dinner party—a horrifying vampiric social ritual where guests were forced to vote on who would be killed—ended when Green T pulled a gun loaded with silver bullets from the CHILDREN'S TABLE and shot the head vampire lord. Archie had to cut off Usk's finger to maintain his cover. Vivian revealed himself and claimed the Heir title. Bowser breathed fire at vampires. People jumped through windows. Waluigi was stuck in the FEYWILD during all of this and he is DEVASTATED he missed it because it sounds like the greatest moment of the entire campaign.
description:
Waluigi was not at this battle. Waluigi was in the Feywild negotiating with a fairy countess about whether shadows count as personal property. So everything in this account comes from Archie, Green T, and Bowser, each of whom tells the story differently depending on who's buying the drinks.

Archie's version emphasizes the political complexity and his masterful navigation of vampiric social dynamics. Green T's version emphasizes the part where he shot a vampire. Bowser's version emphasizes fire. Waluigi has attempted to combine these accounts into something coherent while noting that he trusts approximately forty percent of what Archie says, eighty percent of what Green T says, and one hundred percent of what Bowser says because Bowser is too straightforward to lie convincingly.

The dinner itself was a formal affair in the Shadow Estate's dining hall. Candelabras. Elaborate place settings. Food that the vampire hosts couldn't eat but served to their living guests as a gesture of either hospitality or mockery—and with vampires, those words might mean the same thing. The vampires sat at the head of the table looking ELEGANT and IMMORTAL and HUNGRY in a way that had nothing to do with the food.

Archie attended as 'Darman Knightly,' the fake identity he'd constructed to survive Shadow Estate politics. Maintaining this cover meant suppressing every natural Archie instinct—no fireballs, no arguments with authority, no setting things on fire when conversations got uncomfortable. By all accounts, the effort was ENORMOUS. Archie pretending to be a calm, reasonable person is like Waluigi pretending to be SHORT. The disguise only holds if nobody looks too closely.

Green T had been placed at the CHILDREN'S TABLE.

The children's table. The vampire lords dismissed Green T—a man who can transform into a giant, who survived the destruction of the Tea Leaf Syndicate, who was dragged through a mirror dimension and came back—as a minor figure not worthy of the adults' table. They sat him with whatever children or subordinates attend vampire dinner parties.

This was their mistake. Their CATASTROPHIC mistake. Because Green T used the insult as cover. While the vampires focused on Archie's diplomatic performance at the main table, Green T spent the dinner observing. The room's layout. The exits. The guard positions. The load-bearing social dynamics. He sat at the children's table eating whatever they served and PLOTTING, and nobody watched him because nobody watches the children's table.

Waluigi loves this. Waluigi loves EVERYTHING about this. The arrogance of the vampires dismissing someone to the children's table. The patience of Green T sitting there planning violence. The irony of the greatest threat in the room being the one they didn't think was important enough to watch. This is why you NEVER underestimate people. Waluigi knows this because Waluigi has been underestimated his ENTIRE LIFE and look what he's accomplished.

**The Vote**
The dinner's true purpose emerged during the final course. The vampire lords announced a tradition: a vote among the guests to determine which attendee would be killed.

Just—a VOTE. To decide who DIES. Over dessert.

The vote was mandatory. Refusing to participate meant you were volunteering yourself. Each guest had to name someone, and the person with the most votes would be taken. The vampires presented this with the casual formality of someone suggesting after-dinner charades, except instead of charades it was MURDER and instead of fun it was HORRIFYING.

Waluigi has been to some bad dinner parties. Waluigi has been to dinners where the food was terrible, where the conversation was awkward, where Wario told the same story about his garlic investments for the FIFTH time. But Waluigi has never been to a dinner where the dessert course included voting for someone's execution. The Corvinarus family's social calendar operates on a different moral plane than anything Waluigi has previously encountered, and that plane is BAD.

Archie, maintaining his Darman cover, voted for the Archivist. Waluigi has thought about this choice extensively and he still can't decide if it was calculated survival or panicked finger-pointing. With Archie, the honest answer is probably 'yes to both simultaneously.' The man operates on instincts that he rationalizes afterward, and his instincts said 'vote for someone other than myself,' which is logical if morally questionable.

**The Finger**
To prove his loyalty to the vampire lords—because apparently voting for someone's death wasn't ENOUGH proof—Archie was required to sever Usk's finger.

Usk. An ally. Someone who had fought beside Archie. Trusted Archie. And Archie was told: cut off his finger, or your cover is blown, and blown covers mean blown EVERYTHING.

Archie did it.

Waluigi has complicated feelings about this. On one hand, Archie was in an impossible situation. The cover was keeping him alive. Dropping the cover meant death—not just his death but potentially everyone's death. The finger was the price of survival, and in war, prices like that get paid.

On the other hand: he cut off a friend's FINGER.

You can rationalize it. You can explain the tactical necessity. You can argue there was no other choice. But at the end of the day, Usk is missing a finger and Archie is the one who took it, and no amount of strategic justification changes the fact that trust, once cut, doesn't grow back any more than the finger does.

Waluigi has been betrayed before. Waluigi has been left off team rosters, excluded from parties, forgotten by people he thought were friends. But nobody has ever cut off Waluigi's finger to impress a vampire, and if they DID, Waluigi would have a hard time hearing their apology over the sound of his MISSING FINGER.

The look on Usk's face, according to witnesses, was not the look of someone who understood tactical necessity. It was the look of someone who had just learned something terrible about someone they thought they knew. Waluigi wonders if Usk and Archie have spoken since. Waluigi wonders what that conversation would even sound like. 'Sorry about the finger, but you understand, there were vampires'? Some things don't have adequate apologies.

**The Shot Heard Across the Shadowfell**
Green T chose the moment of maximum chaos—everyone reeling from the vote, from Archie's gruesome loyalty demonstration, from the casual monstrousness of vampire dinner traditions—to act.

He stood up from the children's table.

He produced a firearm.

Waluigi needs to address the question everyone asks: HOW did Green T smuggle a gun into a vampire dinner party? Waluigi has asked Green T this directly. Green T smiled and changed the subject. Waluigi respects a man who keeps his methods private. Waluigi ALSO keeps his methods private, mostly because people react badly when Waluigi explains his methods.

The gun was loaded with SILVER bullets. Silver. The one material that vampires cannot shrug off. The one weakness in their immortal, arrogant, dinner-party-hosting, children's-table-assigning aristocratic existence. And Green T had brought it to dinner in his pocket.

He aimed at Orangus Cornelius—senior vampire lord, Onyx Hand authority figure, centuries-old undead aristocrat who had survived wars and revolutions and the collapse of empires—and fired.

The bullet hit.

The CHILDREN'S TABLE shot the HEAD VAMPIRE.

Waluigi WISHES he could have seen Orangus Cornelius's face. The expression of a vampire lord who has spent centuries being the most dangerous person in every room, realizing that the LEAST important guest just put a silver bullet in him. The moment of comprehension. The fraction of a second between 'this cannot be happening' and 'this is absolutely happening.'

Waluigi would pay—would pay ACTUAL COINS—for a painting of that moment. He would hang it in his bedroom. He would hang it EVERYWHERE. He would commission MULTIPLE paintings in different artistic styles. Impressionist Orangus getting shot. Cubist Orangus getting shot. One of those paintings made entirely of dots, showing Orangus getting shot. The artistic possibilities are ENDLESS.

**Vivian's Revelation**
In the middle of the chaos—because this story apparently did not have ENOUGH going on—the thrall known as 'Vivesna' chose this moment to make a revelation. Vivesna was actually Vivian. Male, not female as the vampires had believed. And Vivian claimed the title of Heir to the Corvinarus line.

During a gunfight. At a dinner party. In the Shadowfell. After someone just shot the host.

The TIMING. Waluigi appreciates dramatic timing more than almost anyone—Waluigi has spent his entire life perfecting dramatic timing—and even HE thinks Vivian's reveal was a masterclass. You wait for the exact moment when everyone is too busy dodging silver bullets to process what you've just said, and you claim a hereditary title. By the time the vampires recovered enough to object, the claim was already on the record. Brilliant. Insane. Possibly both.

Vivian had apparently been hiding in plain sight for—how long? Years? Decades? Time gets weird with vampires. However long it was, Vivian had maintained a false identity within the Corvinarus household, waiting for the right moment to reveal the truth. And the right moment, apparently, was 'immediately after Green T shoots the senior lord with silver.'

Waluigi respects the audacity. Waluigi questions the sanity. Waluigi acknowledges that, in the vampire world, audacity and sanity might be less distinguishable than they are elsewhere.

**The Escape**
Archie and Green T made for the nearest window. Not the nearest DOOR—the nearest WINDOW. They went through it—glass, frame, decorative molding, and all—and landed in the rose garden below.

Waluigi has jumped through a lot of windows in his career. Party exits, sports mishaps, that one incident at Wario's house that nobody talks about. He knows from experience that rose bushes are NOT ideal landing surfaces. They have thorns. The thorns go through clothing. The landing is undignified. You spend the next week finding thorns in uncomfortable places.

But rose bushes are significantly better than a room full of angry vampires, so Waluigi supports the decision. Strategic window exit is a valid tactical choice when the alternative is being eaten by immortal aristocrats.

Bowser stayed. Because Bowser is BOWSER. Bowser does not fit through windows. Bowser does not flee from fights. Bowser does not understand the concept of tactical withdrawal. What Bowser DOES understand is fire, and he employed that understanding generously.

Bowser breathed fire at the vampire lords.

Now, the Shadowfell suppresses MAGICAL fire. Archie's fire spells were useless in this plane—the dimensional physics simply wouldn't allow it. But Bowser's fire isn't magical. Bowser's fire is BIOLOGICAL. It comes from his gut, not his spellbook. And the Shadowfell, apparently, cannot suppress the fire of a giant turtle dragon who is genetically MADE of fury.

The distinction between magical fire and biological fire is academic in most situations. In THIS situation, it was the difference between 'helpless against vampires' and 'BREATHING FIRE AT VAMPIRES WHILE YOUR FRIENDS ESCAPE THROUGH A WINDOW.' Bowser's flames bought time. They created chaos. They forced the vampire lords to deal with a fire-breathing dinosaur in their dining room instead of pursuing the people who had just shot their leader and dived into the rosemary.

**The Rose Garden**
Archie and Green T landed in the Shadow Estate's rose garden—a monochrome nightmare of grey roses and black thorns that had clearly been designed by someone who thought 'cheerful' was a disease. The garden provided temporary cover but not safety. Vampire thralls were mobilizing. The lords who weren't currently on fire were organizing pursuit.

The escape from the garden to the estate's perimeter involved more running than fighting—moving fast through hedge mazes and ornamental arrangements while pursuers closed from multiple directions. Green T's knowledge of the estate's layout, gathered during his time at the children's table, proved invaluable. He'd mapped the exits. He'd identified the guard positions. He'd done reconnaissance while everyone assumed he was eating appetizers and feeling sorry for himself.

The lesson here is one Waluigi has known his entire life: never dismiss anyone. The person you think is least important might be the one who destroys everything you've built. Green T was seated at the children's table because the vampires thought he didn't matter. Green T shot their leader because they gave him time to plan. Arrogance is expensive. The vampires paid in silver.

**Bowser's Exit**
Bowser eventually extracted himself from the dining hall through a combination of fire, physical force, and what witnesses described as 'enthusiastic property damage.' The wall he exited through reportedly did not survive the experience. Neither did several pieces of furniture, two decorative pillars, and a portrait of some Corvinarus ancestor who probably deserved it.

Bowser rejoined the others outside the estate proper, and the group made for the dimensional boundary that would eventually allow return to the physical plane. The pursuit continued but grew disorganized—the vampires were dealing with injuries, succession chaos, and the basic question of what had just happened to their nice dinner party.

Waluigi wasn't there. Waluigi was in the Feywild arguing with a mushroom about property rights. But hearing about this afterward—Green T at the children's table, the silver bullet, the window escape, Bowser breathing biological fire at immortal aristocrats—Waluigi felt something he doesn't feel often.

He felt PROUD. Proud of his allies. Proud of Green T's patience and courage. Proud of Bowser's unmovable stubbornness. Even grudgingly proud of Archie, who kept a cover alive long enough for the moment to matter, even if the price was a friend's finger.

Waluigi missed the greatest dinner party exit in the history of dinner parties, and that will bother him for the rest of his life. But knowing it HAPPENED—knowing that the people Waluigi fights alongside are capable of THAT—makes Waluigi feel like maybe being on this team isn't the cosmic insult he usually considers it to be.

Maybe.

Don't tell anyone Waluigi said that. WAH.
aftermath:
Orangus Cornelius took a silver bullet, which for a vampire lord is considerably worse than a regular bullet—silver wounds don't heal the way normal damage does, and the metaphysical implications within the Corvinarus power structure were severe. A wounded patriarch is a vulnerable patriarch, and vampire politics does not treat vulnerability kindly. Factions within the Onyx Hand began positioning themselves to take advantage before the blood from the gunshot had even dried.

Vivian's claim to the Heir title threw the family's succession into chaos, creating fractures within the Onyx Hand that multiple parties would attempt to exploit. A legitimate heir emerging from the thrall population raised questions about bloodline, about who else might be hiding in plain sight, about the entire social order the Corvinarus had maintained for centuries. The claim couldn't be ignored, and it couldn't be easily dismissed.

The Shadow Estate dinner marked the absolute end of any diplomatic pretense between the party and the vampire lords—from this point forward, the relationship was pure hostility. The vampires had been shot, embarrassed, set on fire, and had their walls broken. These are not injuries that immortal aristocrats forgive. Ever.

Archie's severing of Usk's finger remained an open wound—figuratively and literally—in the party's internal trust. Some costs cannot be justified retroactively. Some debts cannot be repaid. Archie maintained his cover and probably saved lives, but he did it by maiming someone who trusted him, and that mathematics doesn't balance cleanly.

Green T's reputation reached legendary status. A man who had survived the destruction of his criminal empire, been dragged through a mirror dimension, escaped the Deep Mirror, and then shot a vampire lord with silver from the children's table was not someone anyone would underestimate again. Green T proved that dismissal is dangerous. He proved that patience and planning can defeat age and power. He proved that sometimes the most important person in the room is the one you're ignoring.

Bowser's fire proved that the Shadowfell's anti-magic properties had limits, which would inform tactical planning for any future operations in the plane. Biological abilities function where magical ones don't. This is useful information for anyone planning Shadowfell incursions, though Waluigi hopes he never needs it.

And Waluigi, stuck in the Feywild, heard about all of it secondhand and experienced the unique agony of knowing he missed the single coolest thing any of his friends had ever done. Every version of the story he's heard has been slightly different. Every retelling has added details or embellished moments. By now, the legend of the dinner party assassination has probably grown beyond the actual event.

Waluigi doesn't mind. Some stories deserve to grow. Some moments deserve to become legends. Green T shooting Orangus Cornelius from the children's table is one of those moments, and Waluigi will tell that story at every opportunity, adding his own embellishments, making sure the world knows what happened at the Shadow Estate.

Because the world SHOULD know. The world should know that arrogance has consequences. The world should know that the person you dismiss might be the person who destroys you. The world should know that Waluigi's allies are MAGNIFICENT, even when Waluigi isn't there to see it.

WAH!

description:
Waluigi is reconstructing this fight from Markop's account. Markop does not exaggerate. When Markop says something was desperate, Waluigi translates that as 'we were seconds from death and only survived through luck, divine intervention, and Bowser being Bowser.'

## Phase 1: The Drag

Markop regained consciousness while being hauled across stone floors by his tail. Bowser was dragging him through dim corridors while footsteps echoed behind them—Vivian's footsteps, measured and unhurried, because Vivian apparently felt no need to RUN when pursuing prey through a manor he'd spent weeks mapping from the inside as 'Vivesna.'

This is the advantage of the triple identity. Vivian had been a THRALL in this estate. He knew the corridors. He knew the patrol routes. He knew which doors locked and which didn't, which hallways dead-ended and which connected. Markop and Bowser were running blind in enemy territory. Vivian was hunting in his own HOME.

Markop managed to push himself upright enough to ask 'What happened?' Bowser's answer was characteristically direct: 'Running away from that guy.' Bowser had held Vivian off with fire breath earlier, buying enough time to drag Markop to temporary safety.

## Phase 2: The Maintenance Room

They barricaded in a groundskeeper's maintenance room. Waluigi notes the strange details: among the gardening tools and clay pots were ordinary vegetables. NORMAL vegetables. Not shadow-formed, not residue-covered. Carrots and whatever else grows in haunted vampire manor gardens. In a dimension of death and entropy, someone had been doing AGRICULTURE.

This strikes Waluigi as oddly significant. The Shadow Estate isn't just a vampire court—it's a functioning household with servants, groundskeepers, and vegetable gardens. It's ALIVE in ways that the death dimension it occupies shouldn't allow. Someone is maintaining normalcy here. Whether that's comforting or terrifying depends on perspective.

Bowser braced the door with his full weight. Bowser weighs approximately as much as several large vehicles. The door held for about thirty seconds.

## Phase 3: The Breach

Vivian hacked through the door with an axe. Not magic—STEEL. While posing as Vivesna the thrall, Vivian had presumably had access to the estate's tool rooms, weapon stores, and service corridors. He knew where the axes were. He'd probably catalogued them.

The methodical axe strikes demonstrated something important: Vivian doesn't NEED magic. He's trained with physical weapons. He adapts his approach to circumstances. When the dimension suppresses spellcasting, he picks up an axe. When circumstances favor magic, he casts a death beam. This tactical flexibility makes him significantly more dangerous than a pure mage or a pure fighter.

When the door burst open, Vivian entered with the calm of someone walking into a room he owns. Smoke bomb first—thick, blinding cloud. Professional entry technique. Then advance through the concealment.

Markop deflected the smoke and pushed past Vivian into the corridor. Bowser struck from the side—a solid hit across Vivian's head that staggered him. Markop followed with his battle axe, cutting into Vivian's side through the red robes.

Vivian bled. Vivian LAUGHED.

Waluigi has discussed this with Markop and confirmed: the laugh was not manic or unhinged. It was AMUSED. Like someone who had been inconvenienced rather than injured. The Corvinarus bloodline's relationship with physical damage is apparently very different from normal biology.

## Phase 4: The Crimson Beam

Vivian dropped to one knee. Not from pain—from PREPARATION. Chanting began. Magic gathered with an intensity that the Shadowfell's suppression field should have prevented.

'The Shadowfell suppresses magic,' Vivian said. Then, with a smile that Markop described as 'the most unsettling thing in a dimension full of vampires': 'But not this magic.'

The crimson beam nearly ended Markop. Full force, overwhelming impact, armor at structural failure. A whispered prayer to his god produced a divine shield that absorbed JUST ENOUGH to keep him standing. The margin between survival and death was measured in faith.

This is the moment the Shadow Estate became a fundamentally different kind of threat. Magic that ignores planar suppression. A combatant who was invisible for weeks as a thrall. The Corvinarus succession isn't just political theater—it's WARFARE, conducted by someone with capabilities nobody prepared for because nobody knew Vivian HAD them.

## Phase 5: Component Destruction

Markop's combat instincts saved the moment. He scattered and burned Vivian's spell components—the physical materials needed to channel the crimson beam. Without components, the attack couldn't be easily repeated.

Bowser found the necromancer's wand on the ground and picked it up with innocent curiosity. 'Ooooh. Is this a magic wand?' Markop, still recovering from near-death, managed: 'I'm not sure.'

Remi later confirmed: necromancer's wand. Cold to the touch. Death-aspected. The kind of focus that channels efficiently in the Shadowfell's death-energy environment. Whatever Vivian's magic draws from, necromantic tools are part of the toolkit.

Vivian withdrew. Not defeated—his injuries didn't seem to bother him enough for that. Not victorious—his primary weapon had been neutralized. He withdrew because the engagement had served its purpose.

Waluigi believes that purpose was DEMONSTRATION. Vivian wasn't trying to kill Markop and Bowser in that corridor. He was trying to prove he COULD.

The message received. WAH.
aftermath: Vivian retreated into the Shadow Estate's depths, presumably reverting to another identity or finding a new hiding spot. His weeks as 'Vivesna' gave him intimate knowledge of every corner of the manor. The necromancer's wand is now in party hands—a potential asset if anyone can safely wield it, a liability if it's tracked or cursed. Markop's armor is barely functional. The revelation that Vivian can cast through Shadowfell suppression has rewritten the threat assessment for everyone trapped in this dimension. The Corvinarus succession is no longer a background political drama. It's an active hunting ground, and Vivian knows the territory better than anyone alive.

Waluigi is classifying the hellhound engagement as a skirmish rather than a full battle because the fight was brief, messy, and interrupted by larger pursuit forces. That does not make it unimportant. Small fights reveal habits. This one revealed several.

Rattles engaged first, proving again that the skeleton's comic timing should not obscure his willingness to stand in front of danger. Remi opened an empty room because curiosity remains one of her primary movement modes. Markop called her back. She fired two arrows and missed by an impressive margin, which Waluigi attributes to chase stress, bad angles, and the fact that the Shadow Estate had spent the last several minutes turning her life into musical theater.

Dan began by tending Eager, then was ordered into the actual fight. His approach was clumsy. His swing was not. The hellhound screamed and fled into another room. This is the rare case where poor form still produced a useful tactical result.

The skirmish ended not because the party achieved clean control, but because knights and Lyranth arrived and converted the fight into a pursuit. The important outcome was not the hellhound's defeat. It was that the party remained mobile long enough to reach the trophy room and then Tymnas's cottage.

Waluigi's tactical conclusion: Markop remains the group's stabilizing combat thinker; Rattles is more reliable than his bones imply; Eager requires courage training or fewer hellhounds; Remi under chase pressure loses accuracy; Dan's clumsiness can still land if pointed in the correct direction.

# BATTLE RECORD: THE IMP AMBUSH OF HARVESTIDE 29
### Tactical Analysis of the Shadow Estate Cottage Defense
### Filed by Waluigi, Auditor-General of Residential Warfare and Flying Pest Control

Waluigi has analyzed many defensive engagements, but the **29 Harvestide Imp Ambush at Tymnas's Cottage** stands as the clearest demonstration of how quickly a peaceful morning tea can degenerate into an invisible, toxic indoor skirmish. WAH!

---

## 1. Tactical Setup: The Dawn Tapping & The 9-Imp Encirclement

At dawn, Markop Judi was awakened by a rhythmic tapping on the lead-paned window of Tymnas's Cottage. Hovering outside was an imp dressed in rusted miniature chainmail armor. 
- **The Accusation**: The imp accused Markop of murdering the Archivist.
- **The Defense**: Markop argued *"Self-defense,"* noting that the Archivist had threatened to erase the party's genetic lineage from existence.
- **The Ultimatum**: The imp demanded the return of the Archivist's ledger or threatened an immediate assault by his nine-man army.

---

## 2. Frontal Assault: Dan's Sentry Eye & The Porch Defense

When the imps initiated their charge, Markop armed Tymnas with a short sword and stationed Eager, Salam, and Rattles at the front door.
- **The Invisibility Cloak**: The attacking imps activated planar cloaking, rendering themselves invisible to ordinary sight.
- **Parallel Dan's Sensory Eye**: Feyward Dan opened his third multi-dimensional sensory eye, piercing the invisibility cloaking and calling out enemy coordinates to Eager.
- **The Counter-Strike**: Eager executed a high-speed slashing attack on the lead imp, while Salam landed a crucial guerilla backstab that broke the first wave.

---

## 3. Rear Infiltration: The Bathroom Window Poison Ambush

Recognizing that the front porch choke-point was holding, an elite fireteam of imps bypassed the front and infiltrated the narrow washroom window at the rear of the cottage.
- **The Drenching**: Remi Akamatsu, isolated in the bathroom while preparing her gear, was ambushed from behind and drenched in a heavy, burning toxic poison.
- **Remi's Retaliation**: Despite agonizing chemical burns across her back, Remi drew her dual hand crossbows and fired a volley that suppressed the window intruders and alerted the main room.

---

## 4. Kitchen Climax: Markop & The Right-Hand Man

Markop and Tymnas charged into the central kitchen dining parlor to relieve Remi.
- **The Commander's Resistance**: The imp leader—boasting of his status as the Archivist's right-hand man—shrugged off conventional light weapon hits.
- **The Table Execution**: Markop swung his massive battleaxe in a full horizontal arc, slicing the imp commander cleanly in half across Tymnas's circular timber dining table.
- **Last Words**: As he expired on the table, the commander wheezed: *"Tell my wife I love her..."*—a dramatic death monologue that Waluigi classifies as shameless emotional manipulation.

---

## 5. The Phantom Knock & Aftermath

With their commander dead, the remaining imps retreated into the Hedge Maze. However, as the cottage fell silent, a slow, deliberate knock echoed at the front door:
*Knock. Knock. Knock.*
When Markop opened the door, the porch was completely empty—nothing stood outside except the ash-gray fog of the Shadowfell, leaving the cottage in a state of high alert. WAH!

summary: Green T returned to Tymnas's cottage marked by Mazebound residue and, after a gunpoint threshold argument, cut across the grove to Archie. The Scorncrow answered with a scythe from the dark, knocked Archie off his storm cloud, and survived being stepped on by Green T's giant form. The grove shook hard enough to throw Eager off the cottage roof and announce the battle to every witness indoors.
description:
Waluigi is filing this one from the edge of two witness sets: the people in the cottage who felt the grove turn into a seismic argument, and the two men actually in the grove, both of whom are unreliable in different and useful ways. Archie remembers a fight as a sequence of insults interrupted by force. Green T remembers a fight as a problem of angles, visibility, and how long a body can hold a shape before the shape starts spending the body back. Between them the archive has enough to say what happened and not enough to pretend it ended cleanly.

The important correction up front: Green T did not arrive at the grove as Archie's rescuer in any simple heroic sense. He arrived because the controlled storm still needed investigating, the cottage had become a terrible holding pattern, and Archie happened to be in the line where those two facts met. The reunion matters only because the Scorncrow answered it immediately.

## Phase One: The Greeting and the Scythe

Green T found Archie under the storm with exactly long enough for one exchange before the grove objected.

“Long time no see,” Green T said.

Archie, apparently satisfied that the world would provide no more useful sentiment than that, gave the tactical brief in the same breath he used to complain about it.

“The Scorncrow is off his rocker. We have to beat him.”

No map. No measured distance. No clean statement of where the line was. Just the enemy named and the imperative attached.

Then the scythe came out of the dark.

The first serious move of the engagement belonged entirely to the Scorncrow. No warning cry anybody trusted, no stomping approach through brush, no grand declaration. The weapon simply arrived. It flew at Archie fast enough to interrupt the conversation before either man had finished deciding how to stand beside the other. Archie fell from the cloud under the impact or the forced dodge; the field record is cleaner about the result than the mechanism. He hit ground hard. The Scorncrow descended after the throw and tried to end the matter before Green T could turn a meeting into a side.

Archie got the staff up in time. That is the whole reason there was a second phase.

The staff and the scythe met in a contest of leverage ugly enough to count as truth. Archie blocked low and then high, pushing upward until the Scorncrow had to shift its footing. The push did not win the fight. It bought time. Battle records exist because time bought under force is often the only real currency anyone leaves the field with.

## Phase Two: Mortal Limit, Unsuitable Plan

Green T asked whether Archie was all right, which is the kind of question people ask when they already know the answer has lost all practical value. Archie responded the only way he was ever going to: by powering the staff and throwing force straight back at the thing trying to kill him.

The Scorncrow parried.

That matters more than Archie's strike landing would have mattered, because it tells the archive what class of opponent this still is. Parrying a charged staff attack in the middle phase of an ambush means the Scorncrow is not merely durable. It remains technical while angry.

Green T then proposed the first team plan of the battle: Archie makes fire, Green T turns it into a bullet, and the grove stops being a grove. A good battlefield theory should survive contact with the people expected to perform it. This one lasted exactly until Archie reminded him of the obvious.

“I am still mortal like you.”

That sentence deserves to sit in the middle of the record where the reader can find it later. Archie is frequently described by allies and enemies alike as if he were an environmental event with hair. He objected to that reading in the fight itself. Whatever else the storm cloud, staff, prior planar nonsense, and pyromantic reputation have turned him into politically, he still understands a scythe on the ground as something that can kill him in the ordinary way.

This is relevant because it explains the next tactical choice. Archie does not counter the bad plan with retreat. He counters it with a different bad plan he likes better.

A team attack, he suggests. Green T shoots. Archie infuses. Flame bullet or electric bullet. It is exactly the kind of battlefield innovation people invent when they are one part improviser and one part exhausted.

They do not actually get to use that plan in the form stated, because scale changes the fight before ammunition can.

## Phase Three: Giant Form and False Solution

Archie retook height first. He used the storm cloud to widen the space between himself and the Scorncrow, which is both tactically sensible and emotionally revealing: every surviving account of Archie in danger contains a beat in which he tries to create room before he tries to create certainty.

Green T, on the ground, tried to answer with movement and found ordinary movement inadequate. Annoyance did the rest. The record's cleanest consensus is also its least believable one: Green T grew. Not by illusion, not by symbolic description, but physically and disastrously enough that the grove stopped functioning as cover and started functioning as a measurement problem.

He rose over shrub and grove and low tree. He became visible from the cottage roof. He altered the footing of the battlefield by acquiring more of it.

Then he stepped on the Scorncrow.

This is the battle's loudest moment and also the one most likely to mislead a reader. Yes, the giant form landed. Yes, the Scorncrow went under it. Yes, Archie cheered for immediate deforestation like a man whose politics had briefly become landscaping. None of those facts equal victory.

The stomp is decisive only in the weaker sense that it changes the scale of everything after it. The ground shakes. Roots strain. The cottage feels it. Eager later loses the roof because of it. But a stomp that does not keep the enemy down is not a resolution. It is a reveal.

What it reveals is twofold. First, Green T's giant form is powerful enough to make the grove react as terrain. Second, the Scorncrow's problem is not merely surviving damage. It is surviving humiliation fast enough to counterattack with laughter still available.

*WAH! The archive is contractually obliged to point out that “I stepped on it” and “it stayed solved” are two entirely separate lines in any competent report. Children confuse them. Waluigi does not.*

## Phase Four: The Cottage Learns the Shape of the Fight

A named duel becomes a session-changing engagement the moment uninvolved witnesses get physically thrown around by it.

The quake from Green T's giant form reached the cottage hard enough to create a second battlefield of bad decisions. Remi called it an earthquake because no less ridiculous name presented itself quickly enough. Eager climbed the roof because of course he did. One of the Toads saw the giant first. Eager saw it second and reacted with enough shock to fall backward off the roof and onto Dan, who was already one-handed and in no mood to become structural support for surprised people.

This is not cottage comedy. It is battle evidence. The witnesses at the house did not need a visual of the Scorncrow itself to confirm the engagement had crossed from private danger into environmental event. If a support structure loses a man because the offsite fight changes what balance means, the fight has escaped its own perimeter.

Wario's contribution at this phase is, for once, analytically useful. He walked outside expecting to play benefactor and stopped at “holy moly,” which is the sort of involuntary measurement only a reliable coward gives you. Wario does not understate large dangers when they might interfere with commerce. The fact that he abandoned style that quickly tells the archive the giant form looked exactly as bad as the roof witnesses claimed.

## Phase Five: The Scorncrow Stands Back Up

The Scorncrow's recovery defines the battle more than the stomp does.

It came back wrong and active. It needled Green T's leg. It laughed. Bats swarmed Green T's face until his scale became a disadvantage—more target, not more clarity. The branches themselves entered the exchange next, striking with the bodies hanging from them. Green T stumbled into leaves. Archie, who had regained enough position to keep cheering, caught a branch hit and lost that comfort in a hurry.

This is the point at which the grove stops being background and becomes the Scorncrow's extended body. A conventional monster can be flattened and then measured by whether it moves again. The Scorncrow, by contrast, operates in a field that keeps helping it after contact. Bats, branches, swinging deadweight, bad footing, mockery. The archive is not looking at a duel plus scenery. It is looking at a duel inside an ecosystem committed to the same outcome.

Green T's next statement matters because it identifies the cost curve while the curve is still rising.

“I don't know how long I can hold this form.”

That is the sentence of the battle. Everything before it is spectacle. Everything after it is accounting.

His giant form is not a stable state. It is an expenditure. Once that is admitted on the field, the battle stops being “Can Green T kill the Scorncrow if large enough?” and becomes “Can Green T resolve the field before size converts itself into weakness?” No surviving witness suggests that he could. What they suggest instead is that the field began outrunning the body that had briefly dominated it.

Archie's answer—to ask about weapons, then offer the electric spear—shows he understood this too, though in the irritated shorthand unique to him. A tiny pistol in giant hands is not a weapon solution; it is a joke the battle is telling about scale. The electric spear clinking uselessly at Green T's feet makes the same point from the opposite direction. The right weapons existed for the wrong bodies and the right body existed at the wrong size.

That is not failure in the moral sense. It is battlefield mismatch.

## Phase Six: No Decision, Only Exposure

By the end of the recorded exchange, nobody had won the grove.

Archie was still alive, still shouting, still trying to convert terror into forward motion by sheer noise. Green T was still giant, but not indefinitely. The Scorncrow was still standing, and that fact alone is enough to settle the result line. A named battle in which one side gets stepped on by a giant and remains combat capable is not a victory for the giant. It is an unresolved engagement with a very memorable middle.

What the pair did achieve was exposure. They forced the field into the open. The cottage now knows that Green T can enlarge to impossible scale. The cottage now knows the controlled storm reaches all the way to root and roof. The cottage now knows the Scorncrow can survive direct overwhelming contact and answer it with field-wide retaliation. Those are not small gains. They are simply not the same thing as solving the problem.

The grove remained in enemy hands when the recorded phase closed.

Waluigi's ruling is that this battle belongs on the archive because it changes how every later plan around the cottage must be written. Before this engagement, Green T was a suspicious knock in the rain and the Scorncrow was an external monster somewhere in the dark. After it, Green T is verified in the most inconvenient possible way, and the Scorncrow is no longer an offstage threat but a thing that can absorb giant-force contact, destabilize the ground out to the cottage, and keep laughing.

That is a battle result, even without a corpse count worth celebrating.

description:
Waluigi files this as the second engagement with the Scorncrow in a single night, and the first time the party brought a plan. It did not help as much as they hoped, because the Scorncrow does not lose so much as decline to participate.

## The Plan Was Garlic

Markop carried the Skull Piercer and a warhammer, both bought by Remi, both still warm, both covered in garlic. The squad drank Wario's anti-fey elixir and marched in behind the Toads' anthem. Wario arrived on a motorbike to take command and stalled in the leaves. The plan survived exactly until contact.

## The Swing and the Bats

Remi walked onto the field. The Scorncrow summoned a playground swing beside her and asked if she wanted to swing again. Markop shouted that it would impale her. Remi shot the tree instead, and the bats came out.

## The Pinning and the Vanish

Mossy advanced. Eager put a critical shot into the Scorncrow's feet to pin it down. Markop bonked it. The Scorncrow laughed, exploded into smoke and crow-feathers, and said it was not a monster. Giant Green T lifted Remi to his shoulder to spot it; she saw only him.

description:
Waluigi files this as the second engagement against the Scorncrow in as many hours and the first one in which anybody learned anything.

## The Unmasking

The crows took Feyward Dan first. That is a target selection, not a swarm, and it should be read as one. Salam crossed open ground to stabilise him on the condition that somebody keep the frightening thing looking elsewhere, and Archie volunteered by planting a staff in the earth and shaking it. The Scorncrow laughed — *oh, you little thing* — and its crows carried it off the failing ground. Then it offered the swing: a branch, pointed and spiked.

Archie jumped into it. He knew where it would land. Remi was standing right there. It came down on her, and she found herself at point-blank range with a musket and no other move.

The face came off. The blood was human.

## The Mouth

Wario dusted two shadow servants; Markop's swing took the rest. The motorbike came free and Wario rode at everything at once. The Scorncrow laughed, and jumped into the tree's mouth.

What followed was two men solving the same door in opposite directions inside a minute. Archie, unanswered by the friends who had gone in, fired a bolt of fire that scarred the bark, fired again to the same result, worked out that fire is weakened in this domain, and then poured every reserve he had into a single cast until his eyes turned to fire. The tree died and the exit sealed. Markop, thinking he might widen the way, pulled a plate of bark — and the jaws shut.

## The Interior Log

Inside, the Scorncrow's multiattack went to the motorbike before it went to the man: Murder of Crows twice on the machine (16 to hit at disadvantage, 14 damage), then twice on Wario (17, 13), then Shadow Jump as a bonus action to be elsewhere. The brood followed: an ettercap at BOLD 84 dashing at Remi, giant green spiders webbing an unnamed guard (DC 12 Strength), a Web Strand (DC 12 Dexterity) and a Reel dragging him in on a line, and two web attacks putting Remi down. Wario retreated on morale. The guard put a spear into the ettercap for 5, which is the only friendly attack the interior log records.

## The Descent

Markop pried the jaws open again, found darkness and then a pit, and tested it with a torch. The torch came back out of the trunk — and inside, Remi heard people saying somebody was going to burn them all down. They descended anyway, on Markop's rope, in a marching order set with reasons: paladin front, squishy wizard middle, centaur rear. At the bottom was the Skittering Grove, and Markop knew it on sight: the Silent Grove, the Matriarch's forest, cleared by this party on Raventree Manor's grounds and now reached through a scarecrow's mouth. He walked to the stump they had piled the loot on and put a hand on it. Nobody else recognised a thing. In it were the spiders, the wrapped fruit hanging from the boughs, Wario's recovered motorbike that no centaur can ride, and Legion soldiers.

aftermath:
**Result by objective:** the party wanted the Scorncrow destroyed and the tree uprooted. The tree is dead, the Scorncrow is not, and the party is inside the corpse with no exit. Waluigi declines to call that half a win.

**Carry-forward:** Archie has no magic. Feyward Dan has no magic. Remi is webbed and separated. Wario has retreated once on the log and lost his motorbike to the thing that recovered it. The brood never failed a morale check. And Feyward Dan's estimate stands unrefuted — the party has not seen half the Scorncrow's power.

**Open question:** how the Iron Legion got inside a place with one mouth that had to be pried open by a centaur. There is a second way in, and it is currently the party's only way out.

casualties: No deaths on the party side. Feyward Dan to zero hit points and recovered (Permanent Injury Table 59 — Sprained Thumb, one week); Eager to two hit points; Archie spent; Markop bleeding. The giant green spider and every ettercap on the grove floor killed.
summary: The sentry arrangement failed exactly as the archive said it would — the stump was the plan and everyone ran from it — and the grove fight was won anyway: Eager killed the giant green spider, Dan took the shield and fell for it, Archie whispered the first real Fireball on his record over Dan's body, Eager's final stand took one of the last two ettercaps, and Markop, who never left the stump, killed the last one with his fist.
description: Continuous from the sentry arrangement. Archie ran deeper in; Eager followed and killed the giant green spider. Dan, one-armed, dropped the longsword for the shield. Markop watched the party run from the stump and stayed at it, revving the motorbike; Salam fired from the bike; Markop left an ettercap in the dust. Dan was webbed and fell; Archie screamed — the pact's signal, meaning something else. Eager wrestled the ettercap off Dan and threw him to Archie, who missed the catch, held the body, thought about running, put it down and whispered Fireball. Two ettercaps left; Eager's final stand took one; Eager stumbled backwards into Markop ('Hello.'); Salam healed Dan; Eager survived the next hit on Markop's healing with two hit points; Markop pushed Eager aside and killed the last ettercap with his fist. 'What about Remi? We can't rest now' lost to the Toads: back to the stump.

aftermath: The grove is fought through and the party is going back to the stump to rest. Dan's thumb is splinted for a week (Permanent Injury Table 59). Eager has the electric sphere. The Iron Legion appears nowhere in the record of the fight.
waluigiAssessment: The plan held at exactly one point and nobody went to it. The table's own post-mortem — Archie spent every crowd-control spell and everyone left — is the correct one; the archive declines to improve on it.
